title: Enforce region pinning in Smart Routing (Hosted API)
creator: Mina Haddad
description:
Context
- Part of “Hosted data residency enforcement” for Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation.
- Smart Routing must become residency-aware: selection + fallback must respect an org/project/API key’s allowed region set.
- Gateway will return the public error contract; routing must provide deterministic structured context for the decision.

Problem
Today Smart Routing can:
- pick a non-pinned region when load shifts or when the preferred model/variant is not available in the primary region
- fall back across regions during capacity constraints
This violates data residency guarantees for regulated customers and creates confusing behaviors (e.g., attempted US fallback for EU-only orgs).

Goals / requirements
1) Residency-aware candidate filtering
- For each request, evaluate residency policy (org/project/API key precedence per ADR-021).
- Filter routing candidates (region + pool) to the request’s allowed region set.
- Ensure the final selected region is always within allowed regions.

2) Fallback enforcement
- Disable cross-region fallback by default for pinned customers.
- Cross-region fallback only allowed when policy explicitly allows it (flag/field per policy model), and the destination region is in the allowed region set.
- If no viable candidates exist in allowed regions, routing must return a deterministic “blocked” decision (not a best-effort selection).

3) Deterministic decision context + logging
- Emit structured “residency decision context” from routing for:
  - request logs
  - traces/spans (metadata only; no customer content)
  - propagation downstream to gateway for consistent error mapping
- Ensure we never log prompt/completion text in residency logs.

Non-goals
- Implementing the public HTTP error contract in routing (gateway owns this).
- Multi-region replication or data movement beyond routing/logging boundaries.

Proposed implementation (routing)
A) Policy evaluation integration
- Add a routing-time call (or cached lookup) to Residency Policy Service keyed by org_id + project_id + api_key_id.
- Output structure (routing-internal; gateway will map to public error contract):
  - residency_enforcement: enabled|disabled
  - allowed_regions: comma-separated internal region IDs (e.g., eu-west-1, eu-central-1)
  - primary_region: internal region ID (nullable)
  - cross_region_fallback: allowed|denied
  - policy_source: api_key|project|org|default
  - policy_id: stable identifier (ok to expose to gateway; confirm in ADR-022)
  - evaluation_cache: hit|miss
  - evaluation_latency_ms

B) Routing selection changes
- Before scoring candidates, filter candidate list by allowed_regions when enforcement is enabled.
- If primary_region is set: bias scoring to primary region (existing routing weights) but must still respect allowed_regions.
- If after filtering no candidates remain:
  - return route_result = “blocked_by_residency” with reason = “no_capacity_in_allowed_regions” or “model_unavailable_in_allowed_regions” (see below)

C) Fallback changes
- For capacity failure or health degradation:
  - do NOT expand candidate set beyond allowed_regions
  - do NOT attempt failover group expansion that includes disallowed regions
- If the only available fallback is outside allowed regions, return blocked decision instead of picking an out-of-region candidate.

D) Block reasons (routing to gateway)
- Standardize internal reasons (strings) that gateway can map to error codes/messages:
  - residency_block_reason=no_allowed_region_candidates
  - residency_block_reason=model_not_available_in_allowed_regions
  - residency_block_reason=attempted_cross_region_fallback_denied
  - residency_block_reason=policy_eval_failed_closed
Notes:
- “Fail closed” behavior: if policy evaluation cannot be performed and enforcement is enabled, treat as blocked (discussed below under risks).

E) Observability fields (structured log/tracing)
- Add to routing decision log record:
  - residency.enforced
  - residency.allowed_regions
  - residency.primary_region
  - residency.selected_region
  - residency.policy_source
  - residency.policy_id
  - residency.cross_region_fallback
  - residency.blocked (true|false)
  - residency.block_reason
  - residency.eval_latency_ms
  - residency.eval_cache
- Add a dedicated span attribute set on the “route_selection” span (metadata only).

Acceptance criteria
- With residency enforcement enabled and allowed_regions={EU}: routing never selects a non-EU region.
- When preferred model is unavailable in EU and cross-region fallback is not allowed: request is blocked (routing returns blocked decision) and does not attempt US fallback.
- When cross-region fallback is explicitly allowed but allowed_regions excludes US: routing still cannot fall back to US.
- Routing emits structured residency decision context in logs for both allowed and blocked decisions.
- No customer content appears in new routing logs/traces.
- Staging verification: reproduce SUP-28441 scenario and confirm no cross-region fallback attempt.

Testing plan
- Unit tests:
  - candidate filtering respects allowed_regions
  - fallback does not widen beyond allowed set
  - primary_region bias does not override allowed_regions
  - policy eval failure with enforcement enabled results in blocked decision
- Integration tests (staging):
  - org EU-only hitting models available in EU -> success in EU
  - org EU-only requesting model not deployed in EU -> blocked decision (gateway will convert to 409)
  - org with allowed_regions={EU,US} and primary=EU -> normal routing prefers EU, can choose US only if EU has no capacity AND policy allows fallback

Risks / open questions
- Policy evaluation availability: If policy service is degraded, failing closed could increase block rate. Mitigation:
  - caching (short TTL) in routing
  - circuit breaker + explicit “policy_eval_failed_closed” reason to help SRE triage
  - staged rollout behind feature flag per region/org allowlist
- Region identifier mapping: ensure routing uses canonical internal region IDs (see region mapping sheet) so filtering is correct.
- What constitutes “model not available”: use model catalog deployment map; if deployment list excludes allowed regions, classify reason accordingly for better customer guidance.

Rollout
- Behind feature flag: routing.residency_enforcement (default OFF)
- Enable in staging for test orgs (see internal how-to) then dogfood + allowlist customers.
- Monitor:
  - blocked_by_residency rate
  - attempted_cross_region_fallback_denied counts
  - policy eval latency

Notes
- This ticket is the routing-side enforcement only. Gateway ticket (ENG-4833) will standardize the public HTTP error payload and ensure streaming/non-streaming parity.
comments: 2025-02-03 (Ravi Menon): Agree with filtering before scoring. Please ensure we filter both “preferred pools” and “spillover pools” so the spillover logic can’t leak out of region via failover groups.
2025-02-05 (Marcus Lin): Logging fields look good; confirm policy_id exposure is acceptable per ADR-022. Do not log org/project names; IDs are fine. Any debug sampling must remain metadata-only.

2025-02-07 (Sean Gallagher): For fail-closed: add a metric tag for policy_eval_status so on-call can distinguish service outage vs genuine capacity issues. Also add an alert note to the runbook for sudden block spikes after enablement.

2025-02-10 (Elena Popov): Implemented candidate filtering + blocked decision reason taxonomy. Added cache (TTL 30s) in routing process for policy lookups. Next: wire decision context into route_selection span + structured log record.

2025-02-12 (Mina Haddad): Please ensure primary_region bias is implemented as a tie-breaker only after allowed-region filtering. We shouldn’t reorder across allowed regions in a surprising way for customers unless configured.
2025-02-14 (Elena Popov): Wired trace attributes + logs. Added integration test stub; E2E coverage will land in ENG-4851. PR up for review: pr-21507.
2025-02-18 (Amara Diallo): Gateway will rely on routing’s block_reason + selected_region fields. Please keep block_reason stable strings; we’ll map them to public codes and help URLs.

2025-02-21 (Mina Haddad): Merged PR-21507. Staging test with EU-only org shows no US fallback attempts; blocked decisions occur when model not in EU. Marking done; follow-ups in metrics/dashboard ticket (ENG-4846).
